deepdive.sec: Logistics / India-US & China Trade Lane Specialist with Digital Freight & Green Energy Integration

bull_bear.body: Reinvesting profits into scaling CUBOX, PSU/govt bid capabilities, and digital platform (Freight Jar 2.0); no dividend or buyback mentioned; no external funding planned
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Slow adoption of digital freight platform (Freight Jar 2.0); reliance on macro trade lane stability; execution risk in scaling new verticals; potential margin pressure if PSU orders delay or pricing erodes
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, optimistic, and focused on execution; avoids speculation on margins or exact revenue splits; emphasizes diversification, stability, and long-term positioning as top 5 Indian logistics player
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: CUBOX (LCL) is not just a product but a strategic pivot to capture SME and fragmented cargo volumes, potentially disrupting traditional FCL dominance; PSU growth is not just contract wins but a re-entry into a high-margin, recurring vertical after years of dormancy
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Net cash in hand moved from ₹31.6 Cr (FY22) to a peak of ₹52.4 Cr (FY23), settling at ₹45.5 Cr in Q1 FY27.
- Net fixed-asset block rose only modestly, from ₹7.8 Cr (FY22) to ₹9.6 Cr (FY26/Q1 FY27), consistent with the asset-light operating model.
- Sanctioned fund-based working capital limits increased from ~₹31 Cr (FY22: SBI 16 + IDBI 5 + Kotak 10) to ~₹37 Cr (Q1 FY27: SBI 23.5 + IDBI 3.5 + ICICI 10) to fund higher business volumes.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: CUBOX (LCL): Launched 3 months ago, positive market reception, key growth driver; TiGreen (Renewable Energy Logistics): Performing well; PSU/Govt: Growing at 15%+ YoY, now a core vertical; India-US/China Trade: Stable, tariffs no longer a threat; Freight Jar 2.0: Digital platform enabling new business access but low industry adoption
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Slow digital adoption in logistics industry | Tiger Logistics (India) Limited | beneficiary | Medium | Freight Jar 2.0’s early-mover advantage may yield disproportionate client acquisition if adoption accelerates |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Describes itself as a prominent global logistics firm offering freight forwarding, transportation and customs clearance, with 26+ years of industry experience, a nationwide presence, and exposure to Automotive, Renewable Energy, Engineering, Textiles, Commodities, Pharmaceuticals and FMCG sectors.
- Operates an Asset-Light Approach Model, partnering with players worldwide rather than owning transport assets, to deliver dependable, efficient and punctual cargo transportation; self-styled as 'Pioneering End-to-End Logistics Globally.'
- Q1 FY27 saw renewal of the logistics mandate with Bank Note Paper Mill India and a new break-bulk logistics contract from BHEL, which the CMD cited as reflecting 'the trust customers place in our execution capabilities.'
- Client base of 200+, but top-5 customer revenue concentration has run 46-84% over FY22-FY26 (46% in FY26, 50% in Q1 FY27), indicating a scaled yet still concentrated customer base.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Recognition] Multiple 2026 industry awards cited: 'Logistics Company of the Year' (All India Maritime and Logistics Awards 2026), 'Logistics Champion – Mid-Sized Company' (ISCM Logistics Ranking 2026), '25 Years of Logistics Excellence' (Conquest 2026), plus Great Place To Work certification (July 2024 to July 2025).
- [Promoter] Founded in 2000 by Chairman & MD Harpreet Singh Malhotra, a first-generation entrepreneur with prior international automotive-logistics experience, including bringing BMW motorcycles to India.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Margins stable at 6.3% EBITDA and 5.6% PAT due to portfolio diversification; no cost inflation pressures cited; operating leverage emerging from cross-vertical synergies (e.g., CUBOX supporting imports, Freight Jar enabling new clients)
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue growth: 15-18% YoY (FY26); Margin: Stable at current levels; Order inflow: Strong growth expected in PSU/govt (15%+ YoY) and CUBOX (material contributor); Capex/Commissioning: No new capex planned; focus on scaling existing initiatives
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Scaling CUBOX across India (esp. South), expanding PSU/govt contract wins, leveraging Freight Jar 2.0 for digital freight adoption, potential export of logistics model to Southeast Asia
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Tiger Logistics has successfully diversified beyond traditional auto/yarn shipments into high-growth verticals like LCL (CUBOX), PSU/govt projects, and renewable energy logistics, driving stable margins and 15-18% revenue growth guidance; the scaling of CUBOX and PSU contracts now represents the primary value driver.
